$comment: COPY → ~/.paseo-pi-team/model-routing.local.json on EACH host. Never commit the local copy: it holds host-specific model choices. Values below are placeholders — run 'pteam models' on the host to see what each role provider offers, then fill in real IDs (the WebUI routing form suggests the same list inline). 'paseoProvider' names the runtime family AND the role: pi-<role> or claude-<role>. The model reference shape follows the family: pi = '<pi-provider>/<model-id>' (the model id may itself contain slashes, e.g. 'openrouter/vendor/model-name' — Paseo splits at the FIRST slash only); claude = a bare model id such as 'claude-opus-5'. 'thinking' is family-specific too: pi ∈ off|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max, claude ∈ off|low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultracode, and it must be supported by the model (check model.thinkingOptions; for custom pi models in ~/.pi/agent/models.json, a thinkingLevelMap entry of null means the level is silently clamped by pi — treat it as unsupported). Routes may mix families freely: one class on pi, another on Claude, on the same host. OPTIONAL classes SUPERVISOR_GOVERNANCE (must name a *-supervisor provider: the route a Lead seats its Supervisor from) and LEAD_RECOVERY (must name a *-lead provider: the route a Supervisor recovers a Lead from) may be omitted — the file still validates, preflight warns, and the create_agent gate refuses that flow until the class is configured (pteam routing set <CLASS> ...). Every create_agent by a Lead or Supervisor declares its class in labels["team.model-class"] and must match that class's route exactly: provider family+role, model id and thinking level. A class routed to a *-supervisor provider (MONITOR_ECONOMY below) cannot be used to seat a Peer.
